hints: Compare the first and last characters. If they match, they are already a mirrored pair. If they don't, one of them needs a new partner inserted on the other side — which choice is cheaper?
Interval DP: dp[i][j] = fewest insertions to turn s[i..j] into a mirror. Matching ends cost nothing extra; otherwise pay 1 and fix the smaller range. (Same as n − longest palindromic subsequence.)

1. dp[i][i] = 0, and an empty range costs 0.
  2. Loop i from n-1 down to 0, j from i+1 to n-1.
  3. If s[i] == s[j]: dp[i][j] = dp[i+1][j-1].
  4. Else: dp[i][j] = 1 + min(dp[i+1][j], dp[i][j-1]).
  5. Return dp[0][n-1].

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Recursively try inserting a partner on either side at every mismatch, without caching.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Interval DP over substrings (or n − LPS).

explain: For "abb", the ends a and b differ. Option 1: give a a partner and fix "bb" (already a mirror) → 1 insertion. Option 2: give the last b a partner and fix "ab" → 2. So the answer is 1 ("abba"). Shorter ranges are always solved first, so the min is over correct values. A string that already is a mirror, like "level", returns 0 because every pair of ends matches.
recognize: 'Minimum insertions to make it a palindrome' → interval DP on matching ends, or n − LPS.
